story.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password

facts.text: "Agents are starting to do real work on our behalf.

"An agent should be able to do the job it's been asked to do without getting permanent access to everything behind the account, and 1Password provides the trust layer that makes this possible across personal agent experiences."
"Personal AI agents have the potential to help millions of people get more done," said John Torrey, Chief Business Officer at 1Password.
"Reaching that many people takes the industry working together to build agents people actually trust with their lives and work.
That's why we're partnering with companies across the personal AI agent ecosystem, so people can use the agents they choose while keeping their passwords in one trusted 1Password vault."
Whether for personal or work tasks, agents need access to accounts and sensitive information people already use.

Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time.
1Password for Agents lets AI agents sign in without receiving or seeing the credential.
When an agent reaches a sign-in form, it uses a unique digital key to verify its identity to 1Password.
Once signed in, the agent continues the task while the password stays protected in 1Password.
"Claude Duet asks before it signs in anywhere, and soon 1Password will complete the sign-in with the passwords people have already set up, so they don't have to start over.

"Our integration with 1Password gives agents a secure way to access accounts users already have saved in 1Password without exposing sensitive credentials to the model, so you can confidently put AI to work on their behalf."
The 1Password integration gives Claude approved access when needed, so users can accomplish tasks without handing over their passwords.
1Password is launching a new Claude integration for Mac users today.
It’s designed to let Anthropic’s AI agent sign in to websites without seeing your password or two-factor authentication code.
1Password can also broker access across multiple websites during the same task, allowing Claude to complete a multi-step workflow without stopping for a new login each time.
According to 1Password, approved credentials are delivered through a secure channel and injected directly into the destination page.
The password, one-time code, and other secrets never enter Claude’s context, memory, or Anthropic’s systems.
This is useful for things like booking travel or managing online accounts.
The Anthropic partnership was first outlined in March , when 1Password said Claude would gain consent-based access to vault items.
1Password for Claude is available now to Mac users on business, family, and individual plans.
It requires the 1Password desktop app and browser extension, along with the Claude desktop app and browser extension.
Instead of granting ongoing access to a vault, Claude requests the specific login items it needs for a task.
The user can approve or deny that request with a biometric prompt, and the permission lasts only for the current session.
When a compatible AI agent takes control of the browser, the 1Password extension automatically locks down the vault so that only the credentials explicitly approved for that task remain available.

Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials.

“Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said in a blog post . “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate tasks to personal AI agents while keeping control of the passwords, secrets, and credentials those tasks require.”
Agents from Meta Platforms Inc., Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC and Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI will be able to log in to people’s accounts through it without ever seeing the password.
1Password for Agents is aimed at a habit that took hold once agents started paying bills and planning vacations for people.
Most of those jobs mean getting into an account.
OpenAI has connected ChatGPT Work and its always-on Dots agents to 1Password, and Meta’s Muse requests logins from 1Password whenever the integration is switched on.
With 1Password connected, SpaceXSI’s Grok Bot can sign in without anyone pasting a password into it, according to head of product Tido Carriero.
Under the new setup, the password never travels to the agent at all.
A unique digital key identifies the agent to 1Password when it hits a login page, and the request that follows tells the person which account is wanted and for what.
Nothing goes ahead until the person approves it on their own device, at which point 1Password types the password into the page itself.
Duet asks before signing in anywhere, and Anthropic Chief Product Officer Ami Vora said 1Password will “soon” fill in those sign-ins using passwords people have already set up.
The launch follows an argument for tying agent access to individual tasks that 1Password Chief Technology Officer Nancy Wang made last month at Okta Inc.’s Oktane conference.
Speaking with theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, she described an agent as “probably both” machine and human.
Perplexity AI Inc. and Browserbase Inc. are on that list, and their browser-based agents have been connected to 1Password since late 2025.
